html:
The Susquehannock were an Iroquoian people of the lower Susquehanna River in what is now Pennsylvania and Maryland. Their name is often said to mean "people of the muddy river". The English also called them Conestoga, the Dutch and Swedes Minquas.

The English captain John Smith met them in 1608 and described them as tall and well armed. They became key players in the fur trade, selling beaver pelts to the Dutch and to the colony of New Sweden on the Delaware for guns and cloth. That trade put them in long wars with the Haudenosaunee, their Iroquoian cousins to the north, and with the Lenape.

Epidemics and war wore them down. In 1675 Maryland and Virginia militias attacked them, and the raids and counter raids that followed helped set off Bacon's Rebellion in Virginia. Survivors scattered or were absorbed by the Haudenosaunee. A last small community at Conestoga in Pennsylvania was massacred in 1763 by the Paxton Boys, a vigilante mob.
